choices: The mayor and council or city manager
questions.answer: The mayor and council or city manager
questions.excerpt:
City of Delaware City parks, playgrounds and ballfields (hereinafter referred to as
               "city recreation recreational lands") will be closed from 10:00 p.m. until 7:00 a.m.
               daily overnight between one hour past dusk and one hour before dawn. (Ord. No. 9015, 6-6-1983; Ord. No. 23-0227-01 , § 1, 5-15-2023)

Any city recreational lands maybe temporarily closed by the mayor and council or city
               manager when it is deemed necessary to be in the best interests of public safety. (Ord. No. 9015, 6-6-1983)

No person shall ride or drive or operate any motorized vehicle upon any of the city
               recreational lands, except where designated. (Ord. No. 9015, 6-6-1983)

Alcoholic liquors, beverages and any kind of narcotic drugs are prohibited on any
               city recreational lands, except as permitted by chapter 25 of the City of Delaware
               City Code. (Ord. No. 9015, 6-6-1983)

No person shall cut, break, move, take or otherwise injure, destroy or deface any
               trees, shrubs, plants, turf or any building, fence, bridge, sign, playground equipment
               or other structure; nor dump rubbish or other material on any city recreational lands. (Ord. No. 9015, 6-6-1983)

No public assembly or parade, as defined in article IV, shall occur in any public
               place, park or recreational land without the prior issuance of an Event Permit pursuant
               to article IV herein. (Ord. No. 9015, 6-6-1983; Ord. No. 9015, 6-6-1983; Ord. No. 23-0227-01 , § 1, 5-15-2023)

Any person or persons found in violation of this article shall be subject to a fine
               of not less than $25.00 nor more than $50.00 for each offense. Each violation shall
               be a separate offense. (Ord. No. 9015, 6-6-1983)

The mayor and council of Delaware City hereby agree to exercise recreation local service
               function pursuant to 9 Del. C § 1102. (Ord. No. 12001, eff. 7-1-1971)

questions.prompt: In Dover, is drinking alcohol (or carrying it to drink) on a street, alley, or in a public park usually allowed?
choices: No, unless a federal, state, county, or city law specifically allows it
Yes if you are 21 or older
Yes if the container is covered
questions.answer: No, unless a federal, state, county, or city law specifically allows it
questions.excerpt:
(a) Definitions. The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this section, shall have the
               meanings ascribed to them in this subsection, except where the context clearly indicates
               a different meaning: Alcoholic liquor means as defined per title 4 of the laws of the state (4 Del. C. § 101 et seq.). Public place means any place to which the general public has access and a right to resort for
               business, entertainment, or other lawful purposes, but does not necessarily mean a
               place devoted solely to the use of the public. It shall also include the front or
               immediate area of any store, shop, restaurant, tavern, or other place of business
               and also public grounds, areas, or parks. (b) Public places. Except when permitted by federal, state, county or municipal law, it is unlawful
               for any person to consume, or possess with the intent to consume, any alcoholic liquor
               in or upon any street, alley, highway, public way, public building or public place
               within the city. (c) Underage persons. Whoever, being under the age of 21 years, has alcoholic liquor in his possession
               at any time, or consumes or is found to have consumed alcoholic liquor, shall be fined
               as provided for in Appendix F—Fees and Fines. This subsection shall not apply to the
               possession or consumption of alcoholic liquor in connection with any religious service
               or by members of the same family, provided at least one of the members is of age,
               within the private home of any of the said members. Fines not paid within 14 days
               of the day the fine was issued, including the day the fine was issued, shall be automatically
               doubled in amount. (Code 1981, § 14-6.1; Ord. of 6-11-1984; Ord. of 10-25-1999; Ord. of 9-22-2003; Ord.
               No. 2009-09, 6-22-2009)

choices: The state’s division of motor vehicles is notified so that person’s license shall be revoked
The town holds the car for 30 days
Nothing; only state police handle licenses
questions.answer: The state’s division of motor vehicles is notified so that person’s license shall be revoked

More than five times a day
Only if two neighbors sign a complaint
